task: Revise the W2-49 CIT-P (`docs/changes/W2-49-CIT-P.md`) so that it answers each finding of its independent review at `9dd15777`, record how each was answered, and bring §11's order line in line with DEC-737 (staged).
status: DONE — every finding is answered in the CIT-P (fixed in the text, or put to the owner as a question), the 24 CIT-P tests pass, and the commit `0faa0664` exists.
work_completed: Revised the CIT-P in one answer round. Section numbers 1–11 are unchanged. I added §5.5 (tests, code and radius), five owner questions in §7 (F to J), a second reversal table in §9, and §12 "Review and answers", with one row per finding. The frontmatter status stays PROPOSED. New `review_round` and `decisions_staged` lines record the review and DEC-737 (staged), and `decisions_read` is complete. I did not touch the Contract files, the ticket or the tests.

tests: Full run `tests/acceptance/W2-49` (no `-x`): 24 passed, 52 failed. Per file: `test_w2_49_cit_p.py` 24 passed. `test_w2_49_contract.py` 42 failed, red by design: "the Contract's yaml file is version '4.1', not 4.2". `test_w2_49_cit_e.py` 10 failed, red by design: the CIT-E does not exist yet. Nothing was skipped.
discoveries: (1) The plan validator is red at the base before any v4.2 change. I read this from the code and did not run it: line 72 expects exactly W1-01 to W1-50, but `.tickets/` holds 102 files, 50 of them Wave 2 tickets. By default it also reads `~/gov-os-workbench` (line 20, read at lines 59, 158, 207, 216) and `docs/source/` through `git show` (lines 192–193), so no agent may run it as it stands. (2) Eight source-map rows say the moved parts are W3: 235, 237, 248, 251, 256, 280, 283, 292. Rows 252 and 282 (A11, A9) stay correct. (3) W2-27's ticket names the lite A7 and A10 gates in its KPIs but does not cite CAP-44.f as a source. (4) The W1-48 tests read `contract.yaml` only for CAP-61's provider line, which v4.2 does not touch.
risks: (1) The cost figures in days are estimates by WBS §4's method. The ≈ 100 est. LOC for the A7 and A10 build is the CIT-P's own assumption, labelled as such. (2) §6.1's CAP-44.h text is written with the recommended answers to F and G. If the owner answers otherwise, the apply round must follow the answer and the CIT-E must list the difference. (3) If W2-02 closes before Q-14 is answered and Question I is still open, F-2's risk is unchanged.
lessons: The CIT-P tests accept any form of the split item and are loose on wording, so passing them says little about how complete the CIT-P is; the review is the real check. Number source-map rows by file line, header as line 1, as the reviewer did.
proposed_decisions: The CIT-P's questions for the owner after this round, all with Q-14:
- A. Form of a split item: recommend (a1), confidence medium. Option (a3), lite A7 and A10 as conditions inside CAP-44.h, is now listed with its cost (two new ids, 17 → 19 Wave 2 items).
- B. What CAP-43.b lite holds: recommend (i), only the manifest and file hashes, confidence high.
- C. The ten ADOPTED_HEALTHY conditions: recommend (i), a named read of the two protocol sections for the apply round, with (ii) as the fallback text; confidence medium.
- D. CAP-45.a's "signed tag": recommend (ii), a Wave 2 wording, confidence medium.
- E. DEC-090 and CAP-54.a: recommend (i), the Q-14 entry amends DEC-090 in part, confidence medium. DEC-006's PROPOSED status is now named.
- F. The rule for each verdict and who accepts an exception: recommend (i), only the owner accepts, by name, in a `Role: owner` entry, and the auditor accepts nothing; confidence medium-high.
- G. Operational checks as lite conditions: recommend (i), add `gov doctor` green, `gov check` with no RED, and a first `gov close` at exit 0, with CAP-48.b named as not checked; confidence medium-high.
- H. Who builds the lite A7 and A10 stage records: recommend (i), a new FULL engineer ticket with a product-spec worker for the adopt skill, ≈ 2.2 days and 0 days on the copy path if a slot is free; confidence medium.
- I. W2-02's order against W2-49: recommend (ii), W2-02 types the three verdicts plus a list of named conditions and closes on its own, keeping Q-14 off the critical path; confidence medium.
- J. Who closes W2-I017, and in which state: recommend (i), the orchestrator carries the row to Wave 3 at W2-30's close, naming the lite-delivery commits; confidence medium.
unresolved: Every finding was taken: none was refused or left out. Fixed in the text: MINOR-1 (§3.3, §6.1/§6.2), MINOR-2 (§3.2, §6.1), MINOR-3 (§8), MINOR-4 (§8, F-5), MINOR-5 (§7 A, §6.3), MINOR-6 (§2), MINOR-8 (§9), NOTE-1 (§5.4, §6.1, §7 B), NOTE-2 (§5.5), NOTE-3 (§7 E), NOTE-4 (frontmatter). Put to the owner: MAJOR-1 → F, MAJOR-2 → G (the §3.1 table was also changed), MAJOR-3 → H and I, MINOR-7 → J (the undefined "in part" state was removed). Still open: the answers to A–J; P-W2-11, which is not on record at this base (F-5); and F-3 (the Charter and adoption before Release 1), which stays named for the owner.
recommended_next_action: The lead brings the revised CIT-P (`0faa0664`) and Questions A–J to the owner as Q-14. After approval, a fresh lead applies it, and the ticket is then held to close after W2-01 (DEC-737, staged).
